chunks: That good is no good after which there is the Fire, and that hardship is no hardship after which there is Paradise. Every bliss other than Paradise is inferior and every calamity other than the Fire is comfort.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali define true happiness and suffering in relation to Paradise and Hell?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes an eschatological standard for evaluating worldly experiences, asserting that the final outcome determines the true nature of the cause. This perspective, rooted in Shia theological emphasis on the Hereafter as the ultimate measure of value, redefines 'good' and 'bad' not by immediate sensation but by their eternal consequences. Consequently, any pleasure inferior to Paradise is considered negligible, while any trial less severe than Hellfire is regarded as a blessing.
